chunks: As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Yunus, from 'Ali ibn Ri'ab, he said:

I asked Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: “Are the ears part of the head?” He said: “Yes.” I said: “Then when I wipe my head, do I wipe my ears?” He said: “Yes. It is as though I am looking at my father, and on his neck there was a fold of flesh; and when he closely trimmed his head, it is as though I am looking at him while the water was running down over his neck.”

key_terms.أُذُنَيَّ: my two ears, meaning the ears of the person performing wudu (ablution)
key_terms.الرَّأْسِ: the head, whose wiping is under discussion
key_terms.الْأُذُنَانِ: the two ears, discussed here as part of the head in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.عُكْنَةٌ: a fold of flesh on the neck
key_terms.مَسَحْتُ: I wiped, referring to the act of masah in wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: Are the ears considered part of the head in wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of wiping the ears in relation to wiping the head in wudu (ablution). Imam Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام affirms that the ears are from the head and supports this with a descriptive recollection of his father’s practice.
